marks.gloss_en: לא: חד בטומאת מת וחד בטומאת שרץ -- no: the two verses are for corpse impurity and sheretz impurity, so neither is free to exclude regard for sanctity
[the redundant verse comes] to exclude [what is susceptible only by] regard for sanctity
מכלל -- since Reish Lakish's dilemma concerns burning, regard for sanctity must render susceptible by Torah law
by implication, regard for sanctity [rendering susceptible] is Torah law
אלא מסיפא: והבשר -- to include wood and frankincense, which are not food; so regard for sanctity renders them susceptible (a verse derivation; no closer support kind exists)
'and the flesh' -- to include wood and frankincense; are they edible? rather regard for sanctity renders them susceptible and makes them food; here too regard for sanctity renders susceptible
מתיב רב יוסף: R' Shimon 'rendered susceptible by the slaughter' -- even to count first and second; why? it is not food that came in water!
עשאוהו כהכשר מים מדרבנן (= p_abaye_asauhu_kehechsher_mayim)
Abaye: they made it like rendering susceptible by water, by rabbinic law
תא שמע: the grape-harvester for the press -- Shammai: susceptible ... and Hillel was silent; why? it is not food that came in water!
עשאוהו כהכשר מים מדרבנן
one who harvests [grapes] for the press -- Shammai: it is rendered susceptible
Rav Yosef to Abaye: I objected from R' Shimon and you said עשאוהו; R' Zeira objected and you said עשאוהו -- then for Reish Lakish too, עשאוהו כהכשר מים!
אטו ריש לקיש לתלות קמיבעיא ליה? כי קא מיבעיא ליה לשרוף (= p_rl_lisrof_kamibaya)
Abaye: was Reish Lakish asking about suspending? he asks about burning
והאמר רבי חייא בר אבא אמר רבי יוחנן: blood of sacrifices does not render susceptible (= p_ry_dam_kodashim_eino_machshir)
[candidate] the flesh of Lev 7:19 was rendered susceptible by blood
והא אמר רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: abattoir liquids do not render susceptible (= p_ryb_mashkei_mitbechaya)
[candidate] it was rendered susceptible by the liquids of the Temple abattoir
Shmuel: as where one had a peace-offering cow, led it through the river, and slaughtered it while liquid was still moist upon it
